title: Tell me about your weekend
goal: Link sentences into a whole story with subordinate clauses — and master the last A1 rule: the verb that gets thrown to the end.
bekal: using *omdat*, *dat*, *als*, *terwijl*, *toen* with the right word order
building long stories without losing track of the verb
wave: Go back to **unit 18**: run through the irregular verbs from that unit's list, participles only, until none of them makes you stumble.

dialogs.title: Dialog — Maandag, weer
dialogs.intro: The last unit. Budi no longer counts his verbs before he speaks.

lines.speaker: Sanne:
lines.text: Vertel eens, hoe was je weekend?
lines.id: So tell me, how was your weekend?
lines.literal: tell once, how was your weekend?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Druk, omdat mijn tante op bezoek was.
lines.id: Busy, because my aunt was visiting.
lines.literal: busy, because my aunt on visit was.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Zaterdag zijn we naar de markt gegaan, terwijl het regende.
lines.id: On Saturday we went to the market, even though it was raining.
lines.literal: Saturday are we to the market gone, while it rained.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ze zei dat ze het weer hier miste.
lines.id: She said she missed the weather here.
lines.literal: she said that she the weather here missed.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ze woonde hier twintig jaar. Toen ze terugging, miste ze de regen.
lines.id: She lived here for twenty years. When she went back, she missed the rain.
lines.literal: she lived here twenty years. when she back-went, missed she the rain.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: En zondag hebben we gekookt, omdat alles dicht was.
lines.id: And on Sunday we cooked, because everything was closed.
lines.literal: and Sunday have we cooked, because everything closed was.

lines.speaker: Sanne:
lines.text: Zie je? Je praat nu gewoon Nederlands.
lines.id: See? You just speak Dutch now.
lines.literal: see you? you speak now just Dutch.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Als ik langzaam praat, gaat het goed.
lines.id: If I speak slowly, it goes fine.
lines.literal: if I slowly speak, goes it well.

lines.speaker: Sanne:
lines.text: Dan praat je gewoon langzaam. Wij hebben tijd.
lines.id: Then just speak slowly. We have time.
lines.literal: then speak you just slowly. we have time.

notes: **Vertel eens** — *eens* softens a command into an invitation, like "go on" or "so" in English: "go on, tell me".
**Omdat mijn tante op bezoek was** — note *was* at the end. Every linking word in this unit throws its verb to the back.
**Terwijl het regende** — *terwijl* (while, even though) also starts a subordinate clause, so *regende* goes to the end.
**Ze zei dat ze het weer hier miste** — two clauses joined by *dat*, and the verb (*miste*) falls to the very end. Compare the stand-alone sentence: *Ze miste het weer hier.*

**Toen ze terugging, miste ze de regen.** Two things at once: the subordinate clause comes first (its verb at its end), and then the main clause **opens with the verb** — because the whole subordinate clause took first position. The second-position rule still holds.
**Dat meent ze niet** — from *menen* (to mean it seriously). A phrase for "no way", "she can't be serious".

**Toen** and **als**: *toen* for a single event in the past (*toen ik klein was*), *als* for repeated or future ones (*als ik tijd heb*). Mixing them up is a mistake even some native speakers make — but now you know the difference.
**Je praat nu gewoon Nederlands** — and that is the point of this whole course. Sanne's last line is also the best advice anyone can give a learner: just speak slowly, people have time.

grammars.title: Subordinate clauses: verb to the end
body: This is the last big rule of A1 Dutch. After certain linking words, **every verb moves to the back**.

head: Linking word
Meaning
Example
rows: Ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek **ben**.
Ik denk dat het te duur **is**.
Toen ik klein **was**, woonde ik in Bandung.

after: With two verbs, both stand side by side at the end: *…omdat ik moet **werken**.* / *…omdat ik het niet **heb gezien**.*

If the subordinate clause comes **first**, it fills position one — so the main clause opens straight with its verb: *Als ik tijd heb, **kom** ik.* Note the comma and the two verbs meeting in the middle.

⚠️ Recall unit 10: *want*, *en*, *maar*, *of* (=or), *dus* do **not** change the word order. Only the words above do. If you forget, use *want* instead of *omdat* — same meaning, and the word order stays safe.

grammars.title: Building a story
body: With this rule, your short sentences can be linked into a story. Compare:

tables.title: Before
head: Short sentences
rows: Ik ben moe. Ik ga naar bed.
Ik kom niet. Ik moet werken.

tables.title: After
head: Linked sentences
rows: Ik ga naar bed **omdat ik moe ben**.
Ik kom niet **omdat ik moet werken**.

after: Long sentences aren't a goal in themselves. But without subordinate clauses you can't explain **reasons**, **conditions**, and **opinions** — the three things that turn an exchange of facts into a real conversation.
The most helpful exercise: take two short sentences you already know and join them with *omdat*. Repeat twenty times. After that, the verb will land in place without counting.

blocks.text: Reacting to someone's story is an important part of Dutch conversation. Staying silent while someone talks comes across as not being interested; slip in *echt?*, *wat leuk!*, *en toen?* along the way.

blocks.title: Ending a conversation
items: *Ik moet ervandoor* — I have to go (casual).
*Ik ga er weer eens vandoor* — I'll be off, then.
*Het was leuk om je te zien* — nice to see you.
*We spreken elkaar!* — talk soon!
*Doe de groeten aan je familie* — say hi to your family.
*Fijne dag verder!* — have a nice rest of the day.
⚠️ The Dutch end conversations clearly; they don't just drift away. One goodbye sentence is considered a must.

blocks.text: You've made it through twenty units. What you have now isn't just a word list: you can introduce yourself, shop, order, ask the way, make plans, give your opinion, tell about yesterday, and explain why. That's the whole of CEFR level A1 — and in many areas it already reaches into A2.
What matters now isn't grammar anymore but **hours of practice**. Advice that really works:

items: **Don't let them switch to English.** The lifesaver: *Mag ik het in het Nederlands proberen?* Hardly any Dutch person will say no to that.
**Read news written for learners.** *NOS Jeugdjournaal* and plain-language news sites use A2 vocabulary and short sentences.
**Listen while doing something else.** Dutch radio in the kitchen, podcasts on the bike. Your ears need hours, not explanations.
**Find real reasons to speak** — a sports class, a volunteer group, the neighbors. Language used to run your life sticks; language only studied evaporates.
**If you're applying for residency:** the *inburgering* exam is at A2, and this course has taken you most of the way there.

blocks.text: The rest is just the courage to open your mouth. *Veel succes — en tot ziens!*

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks: join with omdat and move the verb.
items: Ik ga naar bed. Ik ben moe. → Ik ga naar bed omdat ____
We blijven thuis. Het regent. → We blijven thuis omdat ____
Ik kom niet. Ik moet werken. → Ik kom niet omdat ____
Hij is blij. Hij heeft een baan. → Hij is blij omdat ____

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with toen or als.
items: ____ ik klein was, woonde ik in Bandung.
____ ik tijd heb, kom ik langs.
____ het regent, neem ik de bus.
____ ze terugging, miste ze de regen.
I'm staying home because I'm sick.
I think it's too expensive.
If I have time, I'll come.
When I was little, I lived in Bandung.
How was your weekend?
It was nice to see you.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: ben / omdat / thuis / ziek / blijf / ik / ik
duur / dat / denk / is / te / het / ik
kom / heb / ik / als / tijd / ik / ,
weekend / hoe / je / was / ?
zien / leuk / je / het / om / te / was

answers: ik moe ben. — het regent. — ik moet werken. — hij een baan heeft.
Ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek ben. — Ik denk dat het te duur is. — Als ik tijd heb, kom ik. — Toen ik klein was, woonde ik in Bandung. — Hoe was je weekend? — Het was leuk om je te zien.
